newsitem.title: EGYPT: Rights group urges "real democracy" in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Rights group urges "real democracy" in Egypt.

text.p: Egypt's main human rights group said on Friday the introduction of "real democracy" was needed to limit the adoption of violence as the only means for change in the country.

The Egyptian Organisation for Human Rights (EOHR) censured the government's attitude to disputes arising from parliamentary elections in 1995, for which the courts have annulled the results for 200 of the 444 seats.

Parliament, which under article 93 of the constitution has the final say on the disputes, has ignored all the court rulings. It has called no new elections and all the initial winners, mostly government supporters, retain their seats.

The elections, in November and December 1995, were widely described as the most violent and most irregular in Egypt's modern history. At least 30 people were killed and election monitors received thousands of complaints of abuses.
EOHR said in a statement that the system should be changed in order to provide the right atmosphere for making Egypt more democratic.

"The government deliberately breaks the principle of the separation of powers when it neglects court rulings, giving unacceptable reasons and justifications which are inconsistent with the concepts of democracy and freedom," it said.
"The EOHR stresses the importance of amending Article 93... This article makes the defendant arbiter at the same time, smashing the principal of judicial supervision," it added.

"Without development (towards democracy), violence will continue to be the only possible way for change in Egypt. Establishing real democractic values in Egypt...is a major means to limit the adoption of violence," it added.
It was referring to a campaign of political violence by Islamist militants, in which more than 1,000 people have been killed in Egypt in the last four years.

The organisation said that the Court of Cassation, the court of last resort for most cases, had so far upheld 200 out of 915 challenges to the election results, annulling the results in those 200 seats. It has rejected 120 challenges and has not yet ruled on the remaining suits.
